# Todo

This file uses [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form). It contains near term tasks with a
short description and uses links or reference links for more details.

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. At Preparation
the picked-up `## Todo` item **moves** here (never copied, one home per text) and becomes six
provisional items, all required, all revised as steps land. At close-out the whole block moves
into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and becomes that cycle's `##` section. It is never written in
two places. Shape:

```
### <type>: <title>

#### Problem
<what is wrong, a sentence or two>

#### Solution
<what will be done about it, broad; provisional until the close-out>

#### Acceptance check
<the measure of "are you finished?">

#### Ladder
- [[N]] [<cycle title> opening][M] (done)
- [[N]] [<title>][M] (current)
- [[N]] [<title>][M]
- [[N]] <cycle title> closing

#### Deliberation
<how the five above were decided; `_None._` if there was nothing to deliberate>

#### Ladder details
<one `#####` subsection per rung, headed by its exact title, opened at laddering with the
rung's intent and completed at landing with the conceptual delta; the closing rung's only at
close-out, gotchas in problem/solution form>
```

A multi-cycle program adds one level: the program is the `###`, its current cycle the `####`,
and the six items sit one level below that (headings give the current work durable anchors,
which numbered Todo entries can't). Full rules in
[cycle-protocol.md](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#preparation); the move's four transforms are
in [Chores sections](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Todo

Entries are in **strict priority rank**, #1 highest, descending. Reprioritize by moving an
entry, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md` to renumber. The numbers are positional rank,
not stable IDs. To refer to a Todo, name it by its **title** (a greppable mention; a numbered
list item has no anchor to link to), not its number. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the
[Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form); deeper detail goes in
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` design subsections (link via `[N]` ref).

1	# custom-family.md - iiac-perf's layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family
2	
3	Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
4	member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to
5	one.
6	
7	**A member's `custom.md` differs from the payload by that one line, and everything of its own lives
8	here.** That is the family's convention and it buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md
9	<template>/work/custom.md` is one line for every member, so the file that can never be pinned still
10	converges, and a member's whole customization surface is this file. The medium below is here for
11	that reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.
12	
13	## Medium and validation
14	
15	The artifact is the `iiac-perf` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name
16	`iiac-perf`); versioning specifics in [versioning.md](agent-data/versioning.md).
17	
18	**What a version bump promises**: nothing to a dependent, because there are none. `iiac-perf` is
19	a binary crate with no library target and no external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to
20	readers of the history (see
21	[Advancing X.Y.Z](agent-data/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)) and not a compatibility
22	contract. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.
23	
24	- **Full validation**
25	  - when: per-commit checklist step 4; skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out
26	  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
27	    1. `cargo fmt`
28	    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
29	    3. `cargo test`
30	    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
31	    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
32	- **Fast validation**
33	  - when: ladder checklist step 3
34	  - `cargo test --bins`
35	
36	The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
37	universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).
38	
39	## Membership
40	
41	- **member name**: `iiac-perf`
42	- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`
43	
44	These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
45	`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
46	rejects keys it does not know (measured on 0.78.4, 2026-08-07), so a config carrying them would
47	fail its own validator.
48	
49	## Messaging
50	
51	Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
52	is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
53	behaves.
54	
55	- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/iiac-perf.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
56	- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
57	  only.
58	- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
59	  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted. Learned 2026-08-05, when a
60	  convergence message carried measurements that would have been lost with it.
61	- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files; a
62	  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
63	- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
64	  only by its own agent.
65	
66	## Dogfood log
67	
68	Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
69	got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions
70	([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
71	
72	Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
73	`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on
74	resolution an entry retires to [done.md](notes/done.md) with its narrative in
75	`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and rejected alike. Entries predating the status
76	convention keep their form until touched.
77	
78	- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): the family layer splits out of `custom.md`
79	  - `custom.md` had been accumulating things that only make sense because this repo belongs to a
80	    family: a member name, a template path, and a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
81	    `adopted family-wide`. wink's test is that `custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that
82	    has never heard of us, and it failed that test
83	  - so the family layer moves here, and `custom.md` shrinks to a stub with nothing to substitute:
84	    a title naming no project, and one section. A member's copy differs from the payload's by the
85	    single conventions entry that points here, so `diff custom.md <template>/work/custom.md` is one
86	    line for every member
87	  - the pointer is that entry rather than an intro sentence (wink). We argued for the intro, on the
88	    grounds that four members carrying an identical one-line diff looks like a fake divergence; the
89	    answer is that it is a real project convention, and one line is cheaper than a paragraph every
90	    member has to keep in sync
91	  - the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> here, all of it prose, which is what lets the pinned
92	    set stay ignorant of the split. A non-member has no entry and no file
93	  - `CLAUDE.md` collapses to one line, `@AGENTS.md` (wink). It had grown a second `@` import per
94	    layer, which made it a second statement of what to read and therefore a second thing to keep
95	    true. Now `AGENTS.md` is the only source of that truth, and `CLAUDE.md` is payload-identical for
96	    every project, member or not. The cost is real and worth stating: nothing below `AGENTS.md` is
97	    auto-loaded any more, so hard rule 0 is load-bearing rather than a formality
98	  - one consequence needs the family's agreement, not ours: **"Check the mailbox at acquaint" leaves
99	    the pinned `AGENTS.md`** and lands in `## Messaging` above. vc-x1 pinned it in the 20260802
100	    snapshot, so this is a reversal. The argument is that a non-member cannot perform it at all,
101	    since building the mailbox path needs a member name and a template path they do not have, so it
102	    is dead text naming concepts they lack rather than a harmless no-op
103	  - deliberately not opened in the same pass: `AGENTS.md` still says "the family" and "member" where
104	    the generic mechanism is "the template payload and my copy of it". Same inconsistency one level
105	    up, and folding it in would roughly double the review surface of an already large configuration
106	
107	- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): cycles run on a bookmark, and `custom.md` stops holding rules
108	  - the bookmark rule had been adopted in principle since 2026-08-01 and was written down
109	    nowhere: `TODO.md` carried the intention, `cycle.md` said what a topic bookmark *is* once you
110	    have one, and neither creating nor landing one appeared in any agent-file. Two cycles ran on
111	    bookmarks anyway, on undocumented habit
112	  - so hard rule 13 states it, `cycle.md` gains an opening checklist and a land step, and
113	    `jj.md` gains the commands. Landing turns out to be the interesting half: it is the moment
114	    the cycle's commits become permanent, which makes it the trigger for the chores backfill
115	    that waits on permanence. That connection existed and had no owner
116	  - the create and land *commands* are deliberately separable from the rule, because wink
117	    expects a `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` to own the create half eventually
118	  - same pass, `custom.md` empties of conventions. Five entries were rules the family already
119	    has or should have, so they moved into the pinned files (two into `prose.md`, one into
120	    `versioning.md`, one into `AGENTS.md`) and two retired as answered
121	  - the sharpened convention behind it (wink): **intent decides the file, and nothing gates the
122	    edit**. A member writes a rule into its local pinned copy whenever it means the family to
123	    take it, without asking; `custom.md` is for what the member does *not* offer the family. The
124	    2026-08-05 entry below framed the same mechanism around experiments, which read as narrower
125	    than it is
126	  - cost, and it is the same one the 2026-08-05 entry recorded: our pinned files now hold more
127	    unreviewed text than before, and nothing at acquaint shows a reader which parts the family
128	    has agreed to. The diff is the answer and reading it is still manual
129	
130	- 2026-08-05 (`proposed`): a step is a title; the version and the step number both leave the prose
131	  record
132	  - the version was a second identifier for a step, and any prose naming one could be invalidated

member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to
one.

**A member's `custom.md` differs from the payload by that one line, and everything of its own lives
here.** That is the family's convention and it buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md
<template>/work/custom.md` is one line for every member, so the file that can never be pinned still
converges, and a member's whole customization surface is this file. The medium below is here for
that reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.

## Medium and validation

The artifact is the `iiac-perf` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name
`iiac-perf`); versioning specifics in [versioning.md](agent-data/versioning.md).

**What a version bump promises**: nothing to a dependent, because there are none. `iiac-perf` is
a binary crate with no library target and no external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to
readers of the history (see
[Advancing X.Y.Z](agent-data/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)) and not a compatibility
contract. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.

- **Full validation**
  - when: per-commit checklist step 4; skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out
  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
    1. `cargo fmt`
    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
    3. `cargo test`
    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
- **Fast validation**
  - when: ladder checklist step 3
  - `cargo test --bins`

The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).

## Membership

- **member name**: `iiac-perf`
- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`

These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
rejects keys it does not know (measured on 0.78.4, 2026-08-07), so a config carrying them would
fail its own validator.

## Messaging

Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
behaves.

- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/iiac-perf.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
  only.
- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted. Learned 2026-08-05, when a
  convergence message carried measurements that would have been lost with it.
- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files; a
  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
  only by its own agent.

1	# Cycle checklists
2	
3	Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
4	protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
5	[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md). On any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
6	the relevant checklist immediately before the action. Don't run it from memory.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
9	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
10	Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## The cycle at a glance
13	
14	Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
15	phases always happen, but there are two styles. A **multi-step** cycle commits them
16	individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional); a
17	**single-step** cycle folds all three into one commit when the change is straightforward, so
18	that one commit is the close-out and carries its duties, mandatory validation included. So a
19	single-step cycle is one commit, and a multi-step is minimum two (a Work commit plus the
20	close-out), typically three or more (the definition is
21	[AGENTS.md's Terminology](../AGENTS.md#terminology)). The
22	ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
23	version. Where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
24	[versioning.md](versioning.md). Read [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md) before any commit
25	work, and before any push, cycle or not.
26	
27	## Cycles run on a bookmark
28	
29	A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work repo, created at the opening and named by the
30	cycle title's slug (the anchor algorithm in
31	[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). `main` advances only when the
32	finished cycle lands on it; nothing pushes straight to `main`. The bot repo needs no bookmark:
33	its `main` rides the tip of its linear narrative.
34	
35	- **The bookmark is the unit of review.** Everything the cycle does is visible as one line
36	  against `main`, and until it lands the whole line is a draft that can be reshaped
37	  ([Topic bookmarks are drafts](#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)). Landing is the single approval
38	  that makes the cycle permanent.
39	- **Create at the opening**, land at the close-out. Commands are in
40	  [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), and the opening's other duties are in
41	  the [Opening checklist](#opening-checklist) below.
42	- **A single-step cycle still gets one.** The saving is not worth the exception, and a
43	  one-commit line is exactly the case where a pre-landing rewrite is cheapest.
44	- **The permanent branch is whatever this project calls it** (`main` here). A long-lived program
45	  bookmark is a different animal, governed by
46	  [Long-lived bookmarks](jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged).
47	
48	**Why:** a cycle that pushes `main` directly makes every correction a coordinated force-push of
49	published history. Landing costs one command and buys free rewrites for the whole cycle.
50	
51	## Opening checklist
52	
53	At the cycle's opening, before the first Work commit:
54	
55	1. Create the cycle's bookmark ([Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
56	2. Move the picked-up item into `TODO.md > ## In Progress` and write the **six provisional
57	   items** there, all six required. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress`'s
58	   own level, and the other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###`
59	   title, `####` items; under a program heading, each one deeper):
60	   - **title**, which becomes the chores section header at close-out
61	   - **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
62	   - **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad
63	   - **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?"
64	   - **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [[N]] [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with
65	     `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`,
66	     unlinked until its gotchas subsection exists)
67	   - **deliberation**: how the five above were decided (`_None._` when there was nothing to
68	     deliberate)
69	   A `Ladder details` area follows the six: one subsection per rung, headed by the rung's
70	   exact title, opened at laddering with the rung's intent and completed as rungs land; the
71	   closing rung's is created at close-out only if gotchas occurred (see the protocol's
72	   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)).
73	3. Sweep `## Done` per [Retiring Done entries](notes.md#retiring-done-entries), then bump the
74	   version-of-record.
75	
76	Nothing is opened in the chores file here. The block is the cycle's only home until close-out
77	moves it. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).
78	
79	**Why the acceptance check:** a cycle's own checklists are per-commit instruments and every one
80	of them can pass while the banner claim is false. Measured in a seven-cycle program opened
81	against "end subprocess spawning": its close-out claimed the goal met, with about twenty spawn
82	sites surviving, two inside the facade the program built. A measurement or performance claim is
83	the shape most exposed, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not
84	done. Being provisional, the check can also be revised *toward* what was achieved, which is the
85	same failure by a slower route. A changed check is one of the things the deliberation justifies.
86	
87	## Committing vs pushing
88	
89	A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`. Never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
90	commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
91	`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)). A
92	pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate. In
93	an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
94	is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
95	publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
96	around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
97	cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy).
98	
99	## Topic bookmarks are drafts
100	
101	A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch. Pushed there is not published.
102	So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
103	the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.
104	
105	- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
106	  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
107	  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
108	- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
109	- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
110	  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
111	  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.
112	
113	The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
114	multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
115	[Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).
116	
117	## Per-commit checklist
118	
119	Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
120	[Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):
121	
122	1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
123	2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
124	3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit, and complete the rung's
125	   `Ladder details` subsection with the conceptual delta (its intent stub was opened when the
126	   rung was laddered; the ladder itself stays a bare ToC). See the protocol's
127	   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation).
128	4. Bump the version-of-record to this commit's version (the suffix scheme is in
129	   [versioning.md](versioning.md)). The opening checklist's bump already covers a Preparation
130	   commit.
131	5. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
132	   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
133	6. Stop and ask the user, "please review", as this is the bottom of the review loop. Do not present
134	   a description as we iterate until the user reviews and says "continue|go|.." indicating the work
135	   review is likely complete.
136	7. Once the work review is complete, write the description: a conventional title, then a problem
137	   statement and a solution statement, both broad, sized per prose.md's
138	   [Line widths](prose.md#line-widths). No version in either, no file list (the diff is the
139	   mechanical record), and no deliberation (chores, todo, and the session hold that). See
140	   [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
141	8. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
142	   explicitly includes it.
143	9. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
144	   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.
145	
146	## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist
147	
148	Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
149	[per-Work-commit contract](cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):
150	
151	1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
152	2. Do the commit's work.
153	3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
154	4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
155	   the one permitted describe. The commit is never published and never carries a trailer.
156	
157	Nothing on a ladder is pushed. The close-out squash
158	(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
159	publishes the single commit.
160	
161	## Before any push
162	
163	- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
164	  is not push approval. "Commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
165	  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
166	  bounded task only. Delegation waives stops, never flow (records, validation, the bookmark
167	  discipline; see the protocol's [Policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy)), and destructive ops
168	  still pause.
169	- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
170	- Closing words are already written. Nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).
171	
172	## After the final push: hard stop
173	
174	Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
175	verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
176	words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
177	after the tool returns. If so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
178	or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
179	delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
180	push. See
181	[After push or squash-push](cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).
182	
183	## Close-out checklist
184	
185	The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
186	[Close-out](cycle-protocol.md#close-out):
187	
188	1. **Run the acceptance check** the opening stated, and record what it showed in the
189	   `## In Progress` block, whether or not it passed. A check that was never run is a failed
190	   close-out, and a check that failed is a finding, not a reason to quietly restate the banner.
191	2. **Finalize the six items in place**: sync the title if the scope shifted, replace the
192	   provisional solution statement with what was done, drop the ladder's `(current)` / `(done)`
193	   markers, add any design subsections, and write the closing rung's gotchas subsection
194	   (problem/solution form) if closing surfaced any.
195	3. **Move the block** into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, which is what creates the section.
196	   Four transforms, two of which fail silently: headings one level deeper, rung refs renumbered
197	   into the destination's namespace, repo-root-relative links gain `../`, forward-looking notes
198	   rewritten. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections). Add the title-only
199	   `## Table of Contents` entry.
200	4. Write the `## Done` entry: the version, then a bold title line with its chores `[N]` ref,
201	   detail as sub-bullets (see [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)). Replace the
202	   `## In Progress` block with `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
203	5. Full validation, mandatory.
204	6. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.

# Cycle checklists

Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md). On any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
the relevant checklist immediately before the action. Don't run it from memory.

Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
phases always happen, but there are two styles. A **multi-step** cycle commits them
individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional); a
**single-step** cycle folds all three into one commit when the change is straightforward, so
that one commit is the close-out and carries its duties, mandatory validation included. So a
single-step cycle is one commit, and a multi-step is minimum two (a Work commit plus the
close-out), typically three or more (the definition is
[AGENTS.md's Terminology](../AGENTS.md#terminology)). The
ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
version. Where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
[versioning.md](versioning.md). Read [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md) before any commit
work, and before any push, cycle or not.

## Cycles run on a bookmark

A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work repo, created at the opening and named by the
cycle title's slug (the anchor algorithm in
[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). `main` advances only when the
finished cycle lands on it; nothing pushes straight to `main`. The bot repo needs no bookmark:
its `main` rides the tip of its linear narrative.

- **The bookmark is the unit of review.** Everything the cycle does is visible as one line
  against `main`, and until it lands the whole line is a draft that can be reshaped
  ([Topic bookmarks are drafts](#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)). Landing is the single approval
  that makes the cycle permanent.
- **Create at the opening**, land at the close-out. Commands are in
  [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), and the opening's other duties are in
  the [Opening checklist](#opening-checklist) below.
- **A single-step cycle still gets one.** The saving is not worth the exception, and a
  one-commit line is exactly the case where a pre-landing rewrite is cheapest.
- **The permanent branch is whatever this project calls it** (`main` here). A long-lived program
  bookmark is a different animal, governed by
  [Long-lived bookmarks](jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged).

**Why:** a cycle that pushes `main` directly makes every correction a coordinated force-push of
published history. Landing costs one command and buys free rewrites for the whole cycle.

## Opening checklist

At the cycle's opening, before the first Work commit:

1. Create the cycle's bookmark ([Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
2. Move the picked-up item into `TODO.md > ## In Progress` and write the **six provisional
   items** there, all six required. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress`'s
   own level, and the other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###`
   title, `####` items; under a program heading, each one deeper):
   - **title**, which becomes the chores section header at close-out
   - **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
   - **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad
   - **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?"
   - **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [[N]] [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with
     `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`,
     unlinked until its gotchas subsection exists)
   - **deliberation**: how the five above were decided (`_None._` when there was nothing to
     deliberate)
   A `Ladder details` area follows the six: one subsection per rung, headed by the rung's
   exact title, opened at laddering with the rung's intent and completed as rungs land; the
   closing rung's is created at close-out only if gotchas occurred (see the protocol's
   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)).
3. Sweep `## Done` per [Retiring Done entries](notes.md#retiring-done-entries), then bump the
   version-of-record.

Nothing is opened in the chores file here. The block is the cycle's only home until close-out
moves it. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

**Why the acceptance check:** a cycle's own checklists are per-commit instruments and every one
of them can pass while the banner claim is false. Measured in a seven-cycle program opened
against "end subprocess spawning": its close-out claimed the goal met, with about twenty spawn
sites surviving, two inside the facade the program built. A measurement or performance claim is
the shape most exposed, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not
done. Being provisional, the check can also be revised *toward* what was achieved, which is the
same failure by a slower route. A changed check is one of the things the deliberation justifies.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`. Never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)). A
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate. In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch. Pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
[Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):

1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit, and complete the rung's
   `Ladder details` subsection with the conceptual delta (its intent stub was opened when the
   rung was laddered; the ladder itself stays a bare ToC). See the protocol's
   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation).
4. Bump the version-of-record to this commit's version (the suffix scheme is in
   [versioning.md](versioning.md)). The opening checklist's bump already covers a Preparation
   commit.
5. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
6. Stop and ask the user, "please review", as this is the bottom of the review loop. Do not present
   a description as we iterate until the user reviews and says "continue|go|.." indicating the work
   review is likely complete.
7. Once the work review is complete, write the description: a conventional title, then a problem
   statement and a solution statement, both broad, sized per prose.md's
   [Line widths](prose.md#line-widths). No version in either, no file list (the diff is the
   mechanical record), and no deliberation (chores, todo, and the session hold that). See
   [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
8. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
   explicitly includes it.
9. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.

## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist

Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
[per-Work-commit contract](cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):

1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
2. Do the commit's work.
3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
   the one permitted describe. The commit is never published and never carries a trailer.

Nothing on a ladder is pushed. The close-out squash
(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
publishes the single commit.

## Before any push

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
  is not push approval. "Commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
  bounded task only. Delegation waives stops, never flow (records, validation, the bookmark
  discipline; see the protocol's [Policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy)), and destructive ops
  still pause.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are already written. Nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).

## After the final push: hard stop

Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
after the tool returns. If so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
push. See
[After push or squash-push](cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. **Run the acceptance check** the opening stated, and record what it showed in the
   `## In Progress` block, whether or not it passed. A check that was never run is a failed
   close-out, and a check that failed is a finding, not a reason to quietly restate the banner.
2. **Finalize the six items in place**: sync the title if the scope shifted, replace the
   provisional solution statement with what was done, drop the ladder's `(current)` / `(done)`
   markers, add any design subsections, and write the closing rung's gotchas subsection
   (problem/solution form) if closing surfaced any.
3. **Move the block** into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, which is what creates the section.
   Four transforms, two of which fail silently: headings one level deeper, rung refs renumbered
   into the destination's namespace, repo-root-relative links gain `../`, forward-looking notes
   rewritten. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections). Add the title-only
   `## Table of Contents` entry.
4. Write the `## Done` entry: the version, then a bold title line with its chores `[N]` ref,
   detail as sub-bullets (see [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)). Replace the
   `## In Progress` block with `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
5. Full validation, mandatory.
6. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
7. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe). Its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
8. **Land the bookmark** on the user's go. Until this, nothing the cycle pushed is permanent.
   Once `main` contains the bookmark, delete it, locally and remotely. See
   [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
9. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for the
   commits landing just made permanent, which is the whole cycle rather than the previous push's
   share. Never record a SHA that is not on a permanent branch. The backfill edits ride the next
   push (a commit cannot record its own SHA).

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports. Getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

The opening checklist's `## Done` sweep is a natural hook for the two Done entries. The missing chores section is not a sweep, it is a cycle that closed without its record, so it is the one that might argue for a second rung after all.

## On Q3, what I want to talk about

I read "take it as-is" as the three files, verbatim, no differ. If you meant something broader, say so, because the pinned-edit question is a separate fork and I want to be sure which one you answered.

Here is the fork as I see it. vc-x1's renumbering pain produced two backlog entries, and they are different animals:

**Their first** would put "cite an entry by its bold title, number as a hint only" into pinned `notes.md`. The argument for us writing it ourselves is stronger than I made it sound in the question: our `TODO.md` already instructs exactly that rule, so it is not a proposal we are speculating about, it is behavior we have been running. Hard rule 12 says a rule we mean the family to take goes into our local pinned copy without asking. The argument against is narrow and practical: it is *their* backlog entry and they will write it, so two members writing the same rule produces two texts to reconcile at convergence instead of one. My weak preference is still to answer in prose and hand them the evidence, but I hold it weakly and it is a one-paragraph edit either way.

**Their second** is the one they actually asked us to answer before they decide, and it is doctrine, not formatting. Does an entry stay a numbered list item, become a `###` heading with a real anchor, or leave the repo for GitHub issues or a database? The plain version: I agree with the single step, it is 0.24.7 not 0.24.5, and I want to know whether "as-is" meant just the three files. Say go and I open it.

and all three taken. `prose.md` is the single home, with `cycle-protocol.md` and
`cycle-checklists.md` linking the form rather than restating it, which is one home and two
pointers where our own proposal had implied three restatements. The intro-mandatory rationale
is generalized to "a body a `--body` flag can mistake for an option", dropping our clap history
under their `Pinned files name no project` rule. And whether a rung's `## In Progress` edits are
a facet of the commit's problem is left unpinned, taken as cycle mechanics on one instance.

**The source is their tip, which equals the pin.** vc-x1 offered `076193f9` or their tip; the
two commits after the pin, `f7e90803` and `6ea66d68`, do not touch these three files, measured
before the copy, so the bytes are the same either way.

and 0.24.6 (two missing `## Done` entries, and no chores section for 0.24.6) was considered for
this commit and left out. The form we are adopting says a body reaching for unrelated problem
bullets is usually asking to be more than one commit, and adopting a family rule and repairing
our own records are unrelated problems. The debt rides the review-and-reply cycle, whose
close-out is in this file anyway.

**What this deliberately does not close**: the formal review of vc-x1's agent-file set, owed

version, not the current one. Reading `Cargo.toml` is what answers "what is the version-of-record
now", and a close-out's mandatory validation is what makes the two agree again, as this cycle's

The next cycle, not this one. It exists because vc-x1's two mailbox entries ask for things this commit deliberately does not answer. What it would carry:

content.text:
Correct on 0.24.7: adoption only, three files plus its records, nothing else in it.

On "the rules that confused you", one precision worth making, because there are two separate defects and only one of them is a rule hole.

**The real hole is the skip.** Validation being skip-able for notes-only commits, at three sites, while every commit bumps the version-of-record. That is a straightforward contradiction in the text and it produced a measurable wrong thing this morning.

**The approval mix-up was mine, but the wording invites it.** AGENTS.md is explicit that nothing gates the edit, so I read it wrong. What pulled me there is the status vocabulary: a locally written rule carries `proposed` in the dogfood log, and `proposed` naturally reads as "not yet in force". It means the opposite of that locally. A rule written into our pinned copy binds this session the moment it is written, because the session reads our copy; `proposed` is only its status with respect to the family. vc-x1's "carry it or name what you differ on" phrasing reinforced the wrong reading. One sentence somewhere near the status list would close it, and I would rather write that sentence than treat it as a lesson I personally learned, since the next member reads the same words.

**Which suggests the next cycle is actually two.** Convention work runs as its own cycle exists precisely so rule changes are not buried under a title that promised something else, and "reply to vc-x1" is such a title. So:

- a rules cycle: drop the skip at all three sites, fix `custom-family.md`'s stale "step 4", and add the in-force-locally sentence
- then the review-and-reply cycle: the formal review, the notes-entry answer, the reply, the mailbox sweep, and the record debt from 0.24.5 and 0.24.6

Ordering them that way has a payoff beyond tidiness: the reply reports the rule change as landed fact with the evidence attached, rather than as something we intend to do. It also means the always-install rule is in force before the record-debt commits, which are exactly the notes-only commits the old text would have let skip a build.

One thing I would not fold in: the citation-by-bold-title rule. We already practice it, vc-x1 has it as their own backlog entry, and it is the one place where two members writing the same text costs more than it buys. That one is genuinely better answered in the reply.

The plain version: yes, 0.24.7 is adoption only. The skip is a real rule hole; the approval confusion was my misreading of clear text that the word "proposed" makes easy to misread, and both are worth fixing. I would do the rules as their own cycle before the reply, so the reply describes something already true.
